claims.head: The Lightning should tilt the ice
claims.body: The Lightning have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Oilers around the middle. Expect the Lightning to spend more of the night in the Oilers’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

TBL.body: Even though Tampa Bay will be without Hagel, the Lightning have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Oilers’ way back in is a power play that gets going.

EDM.head: The Oilers face a real test
EDM.body: Even though Tampa Bay will be without Hagel, the Lightning have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Oilers’ best way through is a power play that gets going.

story.head: A heavyweight meeting
paras: The Oilers have won six straight, and they’re rolling. The Lightning (14-5-2) beat Washington 5-2 on Tuesday. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Oilers are first in the NHL and the Bolts first in the Atlantic (tied for fourth in the NHL).
The Oilers’ record (.804) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.568), largely thanks to their finishing. The Lightning’s record (.714) is about what their chances are worth.

The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest), have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (4th). Edmonton has scored 3.96 goals a game, the second most in the league. As for the Lightning, they ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd) and draw more penalties than they take (4th). They also keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), so the Oilers may have a hard time getting pucks to the net against them. The Lightning wait for good looks, but the Oilers settle for hopeful ones.

Connor McDavid (13 G / 42 A / 55 P in 23 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (21 G / 23 A / 44 P in 23 GP) has a team-high 21 goals, tied for the most in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games. Nikita Kucherov (8 G / 22 A / 30 P in 21 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Edmonton. Jake Guentzel (13 G / 13 A / 26 P in 21 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, tied for sixth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games.
Devon Levi (10-1-0 / .906 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to start for Edmonton, and Andrei Vasilevskiy (10-5-1 / .891 SV% in 16 GS) for Tampa Bay.
The Lightning usually control more of the chances than the Oilers do.
